advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether the `provenance:` continuation line (esp. its free-text justification) should be excluded from the laundering scan to avoid false positives on legitimate external items that cite repo paths in their justification.
evidence: repo_evidence_citations only scrubs URLs before matching (det_attestation_launder.py:73 `scrubbed = _URL_RE.sub(" ", text)`) — the provenance continuation line and its em-dash justification are included in the block and matched for repo paths

Commit message / docs claim: 'legitimately external items (deploy/vote/console evidence WITH a complete provenance line) close exactly as before' — but a repo-path mention inside the provenance justification defeats that
advisory.finding: laundering_gaps scans the entire item block including the `provenance:` continuation line (only URLs are scrubbed), so a legitimately-external [operator-attested] item whose valid provenance justification text cites a repo path/symbol (e.g. `... instrument=static-analysis — verified in src/rebar/foo.py` or `— see docs/runbook.md`) will be reported as laundering and block the close — contradicting the stated AC-4 guarantee that external items 'close exactly as before'.
scenarios: An operator writes a valid provenance line whose justification references a repo doc/runbook or a static-analysis artifact path, e.g. `instrument=static-analysis — see src/rebar/x.py`, and the legitimate close is blocked as laundering

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconsider whether extension-less `docs/`/`scripts/` references should count as laundering evidence, or restrict repo-root matching to code-shaped paths to preserve precision.
evidence: Module docstring frames the detector as precision-first because 'a false positive here would block ADR-0043's legitimate escape hatch' (det_attestation_launder.py:16-19), yet a bare `docs/foo` reference in an external attestation would fire
advisory.finding: _REPO_ROOT_PATH_RE matches `docs/...` (and any src/tests/scripts) paths WITHOUT a code extension, so an [operator-attested] item that merely references a documentation/runbook path (a common, legitimately-external attestation reference) fires the laundering guard even though such a doc reference is not the kind of exact code proof the completion verifier could re-derive.
scenarios: A deploy/vote attestation item whose text points a reviewer at `docs/runbook.md` or `docs/ops/procedure` is blocked as laundering despite being genuinely external

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a repo_evidence_citations test asserting a bare commit hash (e.g. '39de64871c') alone returns [] to pin the documented non-firing contract.
evidence: det_attestation_launder.py docstring: 'Bare commit hashes and Gerrit change numbers deliberately do NOT fire'
test at line 140 uses 'tests/unit/test_scan_scoping.py (merged 39de64871c)' — the path fires, so the hash's non-firing is not isolated
test_external_evidence_is_not_a_citation covers 'Gerrit change 1772' with assert == [] but contains no bare commit hash
advisory.finding: The documented precision contract that bare commit hashes 'deliberately do NOT fire' is untested in isolation: the only commit hash in the suite (`39de64871c`) appears on a line that also cites a repo path (`test_live_grunion_ac19_text_fires`), so it fires regardless of hash handling. A regression where a bare commit hash begins matching would falsely block a legitimate [operator-attested] item and no test would catch it. (The Gerrit-change-number half is pinned by test_external_evidence_is_not_a_citation; the commit-hash half is not.)
scenarios: A future change to _CODE_FILE_PATH_RE or a new citation regex makes a bare 40/10-char hex hash match, blocking a legitimately external [operator-attested] item.
